disagreement_note: The opinionated senior is the outlier, scoring the module 2 points under the other two personas (7 vs 9/8). The disagreement is not about content quality — all three personas approve the plan without executing it and none flags a REVISE-worthy defect — it is about WHERE in the module the objection to 'approve, stop, no execution' gets answered. The mid-layer-competent and fast-operator personas take the Key Concepts bullet ('You don't have to execute a plan to know it's good. Making it good IS the work.', line 66) as sufficient; the opinionated senior reads that same line as an assertion arriving before it's earned, and only settles once they reach the retro's own evidence question in Phase 6 of the core exercise ('What did grill surface that push-back didn't? Would it have mattered?') — a question that makes the STUDENT supply the proof rather than accept the module's claim. The module DOES already answer this objection twice, once student-facing (line 66's Key Concepts bullet) and once trainer-facing (maintainer block Watch-fors, line 146: 'Student asks "why don't we execute?" near P5. Answer: making the plan good IS the work...'; and the P5-deflection push-back script, line 136: 'quote one thing your push-back caught that the second read would have missed'). What the senior's read surfaces is a SEQUENCING gap, not a missing answer: the assertion (line 66) lands mid-module in Key Concepts, ahead of the retro question (Phase 6, end of the core exercise) that actually produces the evidence for a skeptical reader. This does not cross the REVISE bar — no rule requires the assertion to arrive after its own proof, and the retro question already exists and already does the persuading — but it is worth naming as a placement observation rather than averaging it into a single score.
